published_prior_art.cite: ChenXie2026LocalOveridentification derives efficiency for the outcome-bridge-only model, not score lifting for the intersection with adjoint-solvability and moving-kernel restrictions.
MiaoGengTchetgen2018Proxy supplies the standard proximal causal identification argument; this is correctly used as a causal-interpretation reduction.
ChenXie2026LocalOveridentification gives a generalized-inverse EIF for the outcome-bridge-only model; ZhangLiMiaoTchetgen2023Nonuniqueness leaves the full nonunique observed model's bound uncomputed.
ZhangLiMiaoTchetgen2023Nonuniqueness gives selected-representative regular inference and local efficiency under additional conditions, not the two-fiber affine-attainment criterion.
No checked proximal-efficiency source gives this positive nonunique rank-two chart with an actual tangent calculation and strict single-pair nonattainment.
BennettEtAl2026StronglyIdentified and ZhangLiMiaoTchetgen2023Nonuniqueness establish selected-score inference, not the displayed strict gap against a joint-model affine quotient bound.
ChenXie2026LocalOveridentification treats the outcome-bridge-only negative-control model; it does not impose simultaneous treatment-bridge solvability or compute the nested-model gap.

BennettEtAl2026StronglyIdentified provides cross-fitted selected-limit inference and AiShan2025EfficientProximalATE provides increasing-moment proximal GMM, but neither learns the two-fiber affine score projection.
CuiEtAl2024SemiparametricProximal Theorem 3.1 gives the efficient proximal score at the unique, surjective endpoint.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: oeq:score-lifting-completeness; thm:quotient-efficiency; thm:affine-ensemble-inference
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: General tangent equality and the resulting canonical-gradient/inference claims are conditional on resolving the explicitly stated score-lifting question for actual bounded-ratio paths.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The general affine quotient efficiency bound and feasible Wald inference conditional on score-lifting completeness for the restricted joint chart; the finite positive-chart tangent and gap claims remain unconditional targets.

source_verification_receipts.version: Cowles Foundation Discussion Paper 2497, March 2026 revision
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper's negative-control observed model is characterized by the outcome-bridge moment alone, and Theorem 3 gives its generalized-inverse efficient influence function and efficiency bound without imposing the proposal's separate treatment-bridge solvability locus.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:2303.10134, public version corresponding to the 2023 Statistics & Probability Letters article
source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 5-7, Proposition 2.3, Lemma 2.4, Theorem 3.4; p. 23, Corollary B.1
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies nonunique bridge solutions, proves a debiased root-n asymptotic-normal estimator under additional conditions, and states local efficiency only at the further unique/surjective submodel; it does not compute the full nonunique model's efficiency bound.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:2208.08291v3, 1 July 2023 public manuscript; final JRSSB publisher text unavailable for inspection
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 3 gives the all-solution-pair mixed-bias/doubly-robust representation, while Theorems 6-7 give cross-fitted asymptotic normality, variance consistency, and interval coverage under its strong-identification conditions.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of the American Statistical Association 119 (2024), published article
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 3.1 gives the proximal efficient influence function at the submodel where both operator and adjoint are surjective, the treatment bridge holds, and the relevant bridges are unique.
The paper uses increasing moment restrictions to jointly estimate a parametrically indexed proximal outcome bridge and the ATE, and its efficiency comparison is under unique bridge conditions.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Turn the single-pair factorization condition into an estimable diagnostic: give finite-dimensional rank or singular-value conditions under which the projection residual consistently certifies strict inefficiency.

State one concrete nonfinite chart family with verifiable operator continuity, fixed rank, closed range, and score-lifting construction, rather than leaving the nonfinite regime only as a bounded exponential-tilt example.
Add a theorem-level non-subsumption comparison with Chen--Xie that explicitly identifies which adjoint-solvability normal directions are absent from their outcome-only model.

recommended_next_step: Advance to Stage 0, with score-lifting completeness as the central solve target and the finite chart as the unconditional calibration case.
